messages.subject: help plotting multiple datasets
parts:
Hi,
Can anyone give me some pointers for making this plot, I know I'm asking the moon but it is valentines after all. 

steps<-as.vector(apply(t(1:5),2,rep,40))
chans<-as.vector(apply(t(rep(1:4,5)),2,rep,10))
times<-rep(1:10,20)
values<-rnorm(200,0,1)

df<-data.frame(step=steps,chan=chans,time=times,value=values)

I would like 4 plots with steps 1:4 #note step 5 not plotted
x axis=time, y axis = value
In each plot I would like chan 1 shown as a solid line and chan=2:3 as a dashed line
Just to add a little difficulty I would like steps 3 & 4 to have a different y scale to steps 1 & 2.


Huge thanks,
tom

messages.subject: Re: help plotting multiple datasets
parts:
On 2/14/2014 1:20 PM, Tom Wright wrote:
> Hi,
> Can anyone give me some pointers for making this plot, I know I'm asking
> the moon but it is valentines after all.
>
> steps<-as.vector(apply(t(1:5),2,rep,40))
> chans<-as.vector(apply(t(rep(1:4,5)),2,rep,10))
> times<-rep(1:10,20)
> values<-rnorm(200,0,1)
>
> df<-data.frame(step=steps,chan=chans,time=times,value=values)

ggplot(df[df$step != 5,],
aes(x = time, y = value, linetype = factor(chan))) +
geom_line() +
scale_linetype_manual(breaks = 1:4,
values=c("solid", "dashed",
"dashed", "dotted")) +
facet_wrap(~step, scales="free_y")

And breaking this down:
> I would like 4 plots with steps 1:4 #note step 5 not plotted

subset out where step is 5 in the data argument to ggplot; separate
plots by faceting on step
declared in the aes call that is the mapping argument to ggplot

> In each plot I would like chan 1 shown as a solid line and chan=2:3 as a
> dashed line

Mapped chan to linetype, used a manual scale to set 1 to solid and 2 and
3 to dashed. Made up something for the fourth.

> Just to add a little difficulty I would like steps 3 & 4 to have a
> different y scale to steps 1 & 2.

Each facet gets its own separate scale for y because of the
scales="free_y" argument in facet_wrap.

> Huge thanks,
> tom
